source: Sadhu, Shahad, Marino (2026) DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
finding: Generated multi-turn belief-updating tests (default and inheritance reasoning) with verified truth at every turn. Reasoning-enabled configurations clearly beat standard ones. Default reasoning is harder than inheritance. This is the opposite direction from the Kirkpatrick CoT penalty.
numbers: Nine base models, ten configurations (GPT-5.1, GPT-5-mini, Gemma-4 family, Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Qwen3-32B thinking and non-thinking). 9,029-11,682 labelled turns per model. Overall accuracy on the figure ranges from about 47.0 (Gemma-4-E4B) to 83.7 (GPT-5-mini*), with Llama-3.1-70B 53.2 and GPT-5.1 72.5. Qwen3-32B performance falls substantially when extended thinking is off.
limits: Task is multi-turn evidence updating, not a single default question. Per-model overall figures were read from a figure table, so labels are probable. Single team, preprint.
agent_relevance: Extended thinking helps on updating a default when an exception arrives. Do not read the CoT penalty as universal: it may be specific to single-shot generic questions.

source: Sadhu, Shahad, Marino (2026) DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
finding: Confirmation bias is near-universal: models accept congruent evidence but fail to revise when a weakening update (an exception) arrives. Thinking mode almost removes it.
numbers: BiasGap = C1 acc minus C2 acc. GPT-5.1 default gap 0.935 (OR 891, CI 586-1498; C2 accuracy only 3.5%). Qwen3-32B default gap 0.670 (non-thinking) versus 0.008 (OR 1.07) with extended thinking. Gemma-4-12B gap 0.082 (OR 2.9). GPT-5-mini 0.668 default, 0.003 inheritance. Default bias exceeds inheritance bias for most models.
quote: the thinking scaffold has a substantial effect on both the entailment and effect questions
limits: Two cells non-significant after correction. Gemma-4-MoE near-zero gap was an artifact of question order (0.259 when order reversed).
agent_relevance: An exception arriving late is the main failure, so an explicit 'does this new fact defeat the current conclusion' step with thinking is the test to run.

source: Sadhu, Shahad, Marino (2026) DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
finding: Know-but-do-not-output: models label an update as weakening correctly yet keep the old entailment answer. Asking the effect question first changes results.
numbers: GPT-5-mini labels weakening on 95.4% of C2 turns but entailment accuracy on those turns is 20.3%. Llama-3.1-70B: 85.1% vs 14.9%. Reversing question order: Gemma-4-31B effect-label accuracy 0.970 to 0.264; Qwen3-32B 0.803 to 0.414; Qwen3 BiasGap 0.670 to 0.816.
limits: The high effect-label score is partly scaffolded by the entailment question. One preprint.
agent_relevance: Detecting the exception is not enough. The schema must force the verdict to be re-derived after the exception is labelled, and test order sensitivity.

source: Sadhu, Shahad, Marino (2026) DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
finding: Anchoring and irrelevant-update noise differ by model. Llama-3.1-70B mislabels already-defeated chains as weakening; small models change answers on irrelevant updates.
numbers: Default anchoring (kept initial answer when truth changed): GPT-5.1 0.433, Qwen3-32B 0.483; Gemma-4-31B and GPT-5-mini under 5%. Llama-3.1-70B semantic override 83.9% on default C3 turns. Llama-3.1-8B wrongly changes answer on 36.2% of easy off-path turns. Seed variance low: ICC 0.95 (CI 0.938-0.963), CV under 4% for most models, 7.86% worst cell.
limits: Synthetic graphs with generated entity names (pseudoword check in appendix). Open and GPT models only; no Claude.
agent_relevance: Seed-to-seed variance is small on this generator, so a scaffold gain of several points is measurable with 20 seeds.

source: LOGicalThought: Logic-Based Ontological Grounding of LLMs for High-Assurance Reasoning (2025)
finding: A neurosymbolic pipeline (LLM extracts rules, then a compiled ErgoAI defeasible program with overriding rules is queried) beats CoT on legal, tax and clinical NLI, mostly on small models.
numbers: Accuracy CoT to LogT: ContractNLI (1000 items) Mistral-7B 44.4 to 53.4, Llama3.1-8B 44.3 to 50.4, Llama3.3-70B 62.7 to 66.9, GPT-o3 mini 61.6 to 69.2, DeepSeek R1 61.3 to 70.2; SARA (261) R1 62.45 to 72.41. Average +4.41% over strongest baseline, +11.82% over average baseline. Gain in defeasible mode only +5.5% over strongest baseline.
limits: Not equal tokens: LogT makes about 21.5% more reasoning steps. Hypotheses augmented with GPT-4o. Claude 3.5 Haiku gains small (+0.5 to +2) and D&D drops 87.25 to 86.58. Authors not verified.
agent_relevance: An external compiled rule layer helps most for weak models; frontier models gain a few points. Compare against plain CoT at equal tokens before adopting.

source: LOGicalThought: Logic-Based Ontological Grounding of LLMs for High-Assurance Reasoning (2025)
finding: Ablation and trace analysis: the logic-based context carries most of the gain; mode-level losses exist.
numbers: Ablation vs CoT average: logic context alone +2.4, symbolic graph alone +0.5, full +7.4. apply_rule steps 1.08 to 2.66. When reasoning correct, answer correct 48% (LogT) vs 39% (CoT). False negatives 41% to 28%. Mode drops: -0.8 ContractNLI defeasible, -3.2 SARA negation, -0.7 BioMedNLI negation.
limits: Only the compilable fragment is kept (information loss). Abstract says four baselines, body five.
agent_relevance: A rule-application trace step cuts false negatives, the cost side of a 'check exceptions' prompt (gap 7).

source: Castagna, Sassoon, Parsons (2024) Critical-Questions-of-Thought: Steering LLM reasoning with Argumentative Querying
finding: CQoT (Toulmin-based critical questions on a reasoning plan) was judged only by a GPT-4o judge, with no human validation and no token accounting.
numbers: MT-Bench, 40 questions (reasoning and math, two sub-questions each), judge GPT-4o Oct 2024, score 1-10, re-prompted until same score three times. Reasoning standard/CoT/CQoT: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 8.6/8.55/8.95; GPT-4o 8.3/8.2/8.45; Gemini 1.5-pro 8.45/8.25/8.9; Llama 3.1-70b 8.05/7.5/8.4; Nemotron-51b 6.75/7.7/7.3. Math CQoT: 9.8, 9.6, 9.65, 9.55, 9.15.
limits: Text reports +4.61% reasoning and +5.4% math but its own Table 3 gives +4.74, +4.48, +5.71, +5.09 (do not match). Nemotron CoT beat CQoT. Only five models. Mean judge score, not accuracy. No cost figures.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays open: gain is 0.1-0.5 points on a 10 scale with an LLM judge and unknown token cost. Treat CQoT as weak evidence.

source: Castagna, Sassoon, Parsons (2024) Can formal argumentative reasoning enhance LLMs performances? (MQArgEng)
finding: Earlier proof-of-concept from the same group: argumentation semantics over LLM outputs, evaluated on MT-Bench.
numbers: Abstract reports only a moderate performance gain in most categories; no numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract only opened. Exploratory. No sample sizes visible.
agent_relevance: Weak support for argumentation engines around LLMs; no equal-token test.

source: Li et al. (2025, v2) Enhancing Conflict Resolution in Language Models via Abstract Argumentation
finding: Larger-graph ablation (n 26-35, trained on n<=25): intermediate explanation steps matter more than answer-only training.
numbers: Grounded/complete accuracy, Qwen2.5: answer only 0.68/0.56, Q only 0.72/0.59, P-then-Q 0.85/0.78. Llama3: 0.58/0.42, 0.66/0.53, 0.80/0.71. 100 test samples per argument count. Zero-shot GPT-4o grounded 0.54; SFT 0.97 and 0.95. Models without explanations sometimes fall to about 30%.
limits: This is fine-tuning, not an external table at inference time. No test of an inference-time labelling table or solver call. Per-size accuracies not given.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partly informed: writing out labelling steps recovers 12-17 points on large graphs, which supports a visible in/out/undecided table, but no prompt-only test exists.

source: Li et al. (2025, v2) Enhancing Conflict Resolution in Language Models via Abstract Argumentation
finding: Conflict resolution on synthetic argumentation frameworks: SFT models near perfect; base 7-8B models weak. No real-world downstream task.
numbers: CFP/ALSE complete: Qwen2.5-7B 0.71/0.62, Llama3-8B 0.51/0.42, Qwen2.5-SFT 1.00/0.99, Llama3-SFT 1.00/0.99. Preferred: Qwen2.5-7B 0.78/0.63, Llama3-8B 0.45/0.48, SFT 1.00/0.95 and 1.00/0.86. Visual input adds nothing (0.98/0.87 text vs 0.98/0.88).
limits: Authors admit mapping real-world text to arguments and attacks is not studied. Intro wording ('marginally improves') conflicts with Table 2.
agent_relevance: Mapping prose to an attack graph, not computing it, is the unmeasured step.

source: Linna and Linna (2025-26) Challenges for Generative AI in Legal Reasoning
finding: Conceptual paper that names burden-of-proof handling as an evaluation criterion for legal AI and proposes calibration and abstention metrics. It has no experiment on burden or standard of proof.
numbers: No numbers. Maps burden and standard of proof to AULC and ECE. Logit confidence 'quickly loses effectiveness as responses grow longer'. Only first 100k characters read.
quote: Their confidence scores are often misaligned with their actual accuracy
limits: No peer-reviewed venue stated. Calibration claims rest on a citation.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open: no direct LLM test of shifting burden. The proposal to flag 'unproven' fits the schema as an abstain state.

source: Sun, Zappala, Di Maso, Pompedda, Nyman, Santtila (2025) Large Language Models as Jurors, Law and Human Behavior 49(5)
finding: Replicated a human mock-jury study with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and o1. Models gave higher guilt probabilities but far fewer guilty verdicts than humans, which hints at a stricter implicit threshold. The study did not vary the standard of proof.
numbers: N = 2,304 responses; 2x2x2x3 design. Mean guilt probability 63.56 (LLM) vs 58.82 (human). Guilty verdicts 21% (LLM) vs 49% (human). LLMs biased against White defendants, more guilt for five allegations, higher guilt for shorter delays (unlike humans).
limits: Abstract page only. Standard-of-proof wording in the prompt not seen. Sexual assault vignettes only.
agent_relevance: Closest evidence for gap 4: the probability-to-verdict mapping differs between LLMs and humans, so a proof standard should be a stated threshold, not left implicit.

source: Chen, Li, Wan, Yuan (2026) From Statute to Control Flow: Span-Grounded Deontic Trees for Defeasible Scope Parsing (NormBench)
finding: Frontier models silently omit nested exceptions and counter-exceptions (Silent Scope Omission) and decay with defeater depth. Forcing an explicit tree with exclusion guards helps exception-active cases.
numbers: NormBench 2,290 provisions (Chinese and English). Gains concentrated on exception-active, SSO-prone cases; aggregate accuracy can be mixed when structure is unnecessary. The abstract gives no accuracy figures.
limits: Abstract only opened. Preprint, no venue. Not equal-token.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gap 1: an explicit exception slot helps on exception-heavy items but can hurt when none exist, so make the slot conditional.

source: DeFAb: A Verifiable Benchmark for Defeasible Abduction in Foundation Models (2606.18557, current page)
finding: Re-read: the current page compares Direct and Structured prompt styles, not CoT, and reports mostly format failures. No minimality or novelty score, and no model-side held-out check.
numbers: 336 tasks x 2 prompt styles = 672 per model. Success: GPT-5.6 Sol 100%, GPT-6.1 Sol 100%, Claude Sonnet 5 about 81.8%, Sonnet 5.5 about 69.8%, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 46.3%, Kimi-K2.6 45.2%. 1,054 of 4,032 responses failed: 652 contract violations, 366 capped, 36 semantic. Generic repair and bounded search solved all 336 tasks. A circular defeater passed 36 L3 tasks but removed protected predictions in 34; the verifier rejected those 34.
limits: Single sample per cell; the paper says it is not a controlled cross-provider ranking. Source is Gene Ontology only. The earlier 'best frontier 65% on L2' figure is not on this version.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: a symbolic verifier catches over-broad exceptions. A model-side held-out check was not tested. Format contract failure is a major hazard.

source: Sadhu et al. (2026) Verdict Without the Rule: Diagnosing and Auditing Regulatory Rule Sensitivity in LLM Compliance Systems
finding: Verdicts often do not change when the governing rule is deleted, swapped or negated. Prompting did not close the gap.
numbers: Five LLMs, 20 domains. General models 90-92% accuracy; guard model 51%. Insensitivity concentrated in easy cases; when deletion flips a correct prediction, models track it. No mitigation figures on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract only opened. Same first author as DERELAB.
agent_relevance: The agent should state which rule produced the verdict; accuracy alone does not show rule grounding.
